analysis:
The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md. Per the patch excerpt, three hunks change: the 'Last updated' date (line 3), the CI runner description (base lines 1243-1247, outside the supplied text units), and a CI routing/test description (base 1807-1809, also outside the supplied text). Supplied units cover base lines 1-927, so the actual edited content at ~1243 and ~1807 was seen only in the patch excerpt. The excerpt is truncated, so I cannot rule out further unseen changes.

I saw no executable code, no authorization, attestation, encryption, cache-storage or coordinator-contract behavior changes, and no secrets. The units I could inspect (date bump, test instructions) do not touch the T-041 cache controls. The T-041 mentions of DARKBLOOM_SSD_TEST_TMPDIR and 'never use production cache roots/keys' are unchanged context and consistent with the threat model.

The CI wording change (Blacksmith runners to 'macOS CI runners', with routed-job lanes, fallback, timeout and read-only permissions) is documentation only. Any real change to runner routing or permissions would live in workflows or scripts (scripts/cluster-test-plan.py, the CI routing workflows, build.md#ci-runner-routing), which are not in this batch. The docs claim that release workflows stay on literal Blacksmith runners, but that claim is unverified here. Integration should confirm that the corresponding workflow changes, if any exist in the PR, keep release/signing jobs on trusted runners, because the build-integrity assets (A-011, A-017) depend on that. This is an unverified external contract, not a finding. The doc edit itself does not regress any threat-model asset.
